svg.title: Ripple - compare size before cutting silver
svg.text: Ripple - compare size before cutting silver
All silhouettes are 1:1 on this page. Black bands show the actual round-wire diameter.
PRINT AT ACTUAL SIZE / 100% - no Fit, Shrink, or borderless enlargement.
35 mm max / 1.0 mm wire
Body: 32.6 x 35.0 mm
40 mm max / 1.0 mm wire
Body: 37.3 x 40.0 mm
45 mm max / 1.0 mm wire
Body: 41.9 x 45.0 mm
Same 40 mm maximum body size - compare the two wire diameters
0.9 mm wire
1.0 mm wire
Recommended first prototype: 40 mm maximum body size with 1.0 mm sterling wire.
The large center stays open (about 23.6 mm clear circular opening at 40 mm / 1.0 mm).
0.9 mm looks lighter and bends more easily. 1.0 mm gives more stiffness at the same temper.
35 mm crowds the close-running sections; 45 mm offers more space but is visibly larger.
The unchanged design has 22 centerline crossings. This is NOT a plan to solder all 22.
Round wires cannot share a plane at a crossing: agree over/under positions and joints first.
Choose loop closures and attachment hardware with the maker; neither is specified here.
Start with roughly 120 mm per loop for fitting; exact lengths on the other sheets exclude
all joint / over-under / bail allowance. About 0.6 m of wire leaves some spare for one trial.
Try inexpensive wire of the same diameter first. Sterling temper and heat affect spring-back.
Do not alter individual curves to make them fit. Overall size is scaled uniformly.
Read docs/pendant-printing.md for sources, print checks and construction limitations.
50.00 mm between end-tick centers
Square: 10.00 x 10.00 mm between line centers.
Measure BOTH axes before bending. Printer accuracy is not guaranteed.
Cold-forming guide only. Do not solder on paper. Bail, joint design and allowances are not included.
